quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you easily. Reflective clothing also helps make you more visible.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both the front and rear brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of the lane. This is the safest position. Riding too close to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding too far away may cause the other driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a method used to maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before you turn. Look where you want to go. Lean your motorcycle in the right direction. Gently increase speed through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: Pointed with your toes aiming downward.

questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward. Your toes could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: To minimize the potential for fatigue, you should:
questions.explanation: Take breaks often during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may make you feel alert at first, but you will crash when it wears off. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect yourself from wind and weather, which make fatigue worse on long trips.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards when you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: At night, how can you tell if there are bumps in the road ahead when riding behind another vehicle?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping against the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: At night, watch the vehicle ahead of you to understand road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be placed?

options.text: At the front leading the group.
Near the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front, behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see your mechanical turn signals, what should you do?

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to signal your turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your mechanical signals hard to see. Clear communication with other drivers is very important.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: You know they have seen you.
It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver has seen you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, how should riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, what should you do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: What sign shows your front tire is flat?
questions.explanation: If your steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding right away and check your tires.

questions.question: What should you do when lights flash at a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and look both ways.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When a railroad crossing has flashing lights, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times, day or night.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A good clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It stops others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a problem occurs.

questions.question: When cars merge from an entrance ramp, what should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Never assume the drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Never assume they see you. Change lanes away from them if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: Motorcycle boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How can you improve your chances of being seen?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on at all times.
